title: Explore a lakehouse table
summary: Query files through table semantics on a trips dataset.
scenario: A city bike-share dumps raw trips into the lake hourly; analysts read them through a table.
objective: Prove you can read lake files through SQL.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE trips (id INT, city TEXT, started_at TIMESTAMP);
seedSql: INSERT INTO trips VALUES (1, 'Oslo', NOW()), (2, 'Lima', NOW());

engineNotes.postgresql: Any version 14+ works for this lab.

outcomes: Row counts over lake files via SQL
checks: COUNT query returns exactly one row

steps.title: Count the trips
steps.instructions: Count all rows in the `trips` table.
steps.validation: Exactly one row with one column.

steps.title: Per-city counts
steps.solution: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM trips GROUP BY city;

solutionExplanation: Both steps are aggregates; the second adds a grouping key.
